entries.subject: URGENT: PAN auth transport divergence is a live credential-exposure defect, not a benign inconsistency
entries.text:
AC-1..AC-3 complete, AC-5/AC-6 complete, merged as PR #148 (squash 52e77a9), no auth/transport code behavior changed. Full findings: docs/design/PAN_AUTH_TRANSPORT_CONVERGENCE_AUDIT.md.

Severity call (AC-3): URGENT. The older runtime path -- panorama/panorama_runtime_runner.py::get_api_key/op_cmd/get_devices, which is the live --only panorama/all collection path and is also reused as-is by panorama/panorama_recovery_collector.py's RB.2 device-state recovery collector -- sends the PAN admin username, password, and every subsequent session API key as HTTPS GET URL query parameters. The newer path -- configuration/panorama_config_collector.py::_keygen/api_post, used by --only pan-config/all and by panorama/preflight_collector.py's OP.0b preflight collector -- already fixed this deliberately (POST body for credentials, X-PAN-KEY header for the session key), with an inline comment ('Credentials are POST body fields, never URL query parameters.') and evidence-store provenance recording the choice. The fix was never back-ported to the older path. This repo's own register_sensitive_value() redaction only covers this application's own log output; it has no reach into the PAN device's server-side httpd logs or any TLS-terminating intermediary the URL passes through, where the credential and key are already exposed on the wire before this process logs anything.

Per AC-3 and this movement's invariant, implementation-thinking stopped here -- no fix attempted or proposed. AC-4 (convergence design) is superseded per its own 'if not urgent' condition; the audit doc records that the newer path's _keygen/api_post pattern is already the target shape for whoever is directed to build the eventual fix, but does not design or authorize it. Per the backlog note's own original instruction, any fix still requires a dedicated security build together with a TLS trust review before implementation, regardless of urgency -- this RELAY_NOTE is asking for a Product Owner decision on how urgently to schedule that build, not for permission to implement now.

Validation: full regression run in the foreground with an explicit long timeout, awaited to actual completion twice (once before an unrelated self-inflicted DLP-scan trip from the audit doc's own prose was fixed, once after): py -m pytest -q -n auto --dist worksteal, 3092 passed, 25 skipped, 2 failed both times -- both failures pre-existing/unrelated (test_dev_0_5b_auth_consumer_canonical_config.py's repo-wide DLP text-scan tripping on project/build_history.json), confirmed identical finding-count (3) against a clean stashed baseline. git diff --check clean. Repository privacy gate initially blocked push on local pytest-run-generated runtime artifacts (data/.support_hmac.key, data/, logs/ -- gitignored, not committed, this worktree's own test-run byproducts); removed them (regeneratable, untracked) and the gate passed clean on retry. PR #148 CI (validate) passed; full-regression job skipped by CI's own path filtering for a docs+backlog-note-only change.
